correct_completion: the new policy has reduced costs significantly.
full_sentence: It is widely reported that the new policy has reduced costs significantly.
acceptable_variants: the new policy has lowered costs considerably.
the new policy has cut costs substantially.

options.why_wrong: The word order is wrong. In a that-clause the subject must come before the verb.

options.text: that the policy reduce costs significantly.
options.why_wrong: The stem already ends with 'that', so repeating it creates a double connector.

options.text: the policy would reduce costs, if it were approved.
options.why_wrong: This introduces a conditional, which the impersonal reporting frame does not call for.

options.text: the new policy has reduced costs significantly.

grammar_focus: Impersonal passive reporting structure ('it is reported that') followed by a present perfect that-clause
explanation: The impersonal passive 'it is reported that' is followed by a full finite clause with its own subject and verb. The present perfect shows a result that is relevant to the present. Speakers whose first language uses a different reporting pattern may be tempted to use a bare infinitive or a repeated connector, so practise the full that-clause form.
translation: Há amplos relatos de que a nova política reduziu os custos de forma significativa.
